# Context: reduction (jix/src/ops/reduction/)

Scope: the non-test parts of `jix/src/ops/reduction/{common,arith,min_max,variance,bools,custom,mod}.rs`
(tests start at common.rs:1422, arith.rs:615, min_max.rs:448, variance.rs:514, bools.rs:156,
custom.rs:337). Until #97 (49167e0) this was one file, `ops/reduction.rs`; the split was a pure move.
Since 6dbeb15 only the driver in common.rs changed in logic (#100 read cache, #103 `Index`, #104
`OutBuf`); the kernel files are unchanged apart from paths. Paths below are relative to
`jix/src/ops/reduction/` unless a directory is given.

## Purpose

Lazy reductions over one or more dims: `Max`, `Min`, `ArgMax`, `ArgMin` (single dim; min_max.rs),
`Sum`, `Product`, `Mean` (arith.rs), `Variance`, `StandardDeviation` (variance.rs), `All`, `Any`
(bools.rs) and the user-closure `Reduce` / `Array::reduce_unordered` (custom.rs; `Fold` at
custom.rs:141-298 and `Array::fold` at 317-334 are commented out - ignore them). Each public op is a
macro-made newtype (common.rs:1280-1380) over `ReductionOp<S, K>` (common.rs:9-19) plus a
`ReductionOpKernel<T>` impl (trait common.rs:20-114). One driver (`read_data_impl`, common.rs:330-606)
streams the input in bulks/tiles and folds into per-output-cell states; `reduce_tile_impl` (660-755)
picks a one-cell (pairwise/lanes) or multi-cell fold (772-1125); `finalize_states` (1136-1269) turns
states into outputs. Scalar traits (`jix::scalar::Sum/Product/Mean/ArgMax/ArgMin/Variance`) live in
the `traits` modules (arith.rs:8-319, min_max.rs:8-86, variance.rs:8-289; re-exported mod.rs:30-34).

## Contracts

### Provided to callers

- `ReductionOp::new` (common.rs:116-217): rejects a zero-sized output dtype (128); every dim must be
  `< ndim` and unique (131-141), else `InvalidArgument`; dim order is irrelevant (bool mask); `dims=[]`
  is legal = no reduction (each cell `finalize(init(x), 1)`). `SUPPORTS_EMPTY == false` kernels reject
  any reduced dim of extent 0 (147-158). Output shape = kept dims in original order (160-170), checked
  with `check_shape_overflow(shape, max(output itemsize, size_of State))` (171-172). Spec: block shape,
  fixed dims, scale weights, `read_layout_order` filtered to kept dims and renumbered (181-207);
  `element_cost` computed in f64 (175-179, K73 fixed); flags cleared (278-283). Cache ids: inner ids
  merged then taken as this op's `CacheScope`; own `cache_id` added as "potentially cached" (209-212).
- `read_data` (240-267): goes through `context.read_cached(self.cache_id, ...)` (a hit returns the
  cached result: shared read-only buffer to a pull, copy to a push), then enters `self.cache_scope` for
  the inner reads and calls `read_data_dispatch` (293-332; `InnerD` static for 1-4 input dims, `DimDyn`
  for 0 and 5-8). Standard pull/push contract; every output cell is written exactly once (by finalize,
  or in place when states live in `out` and `NEEDS_FINALIZE == false`, 1155-1161).
- An `Index` is never empty (storage/index.rs:10-19, sizes are `NonZeroUsize`), so the old
  empty-output early return is now `debug_assert!(out_nitems != 0)` (412-413); Array entry points
  short-circuit empty regions (array/read.rs:207, 318, 386, 451).
- Per-cell semantics (comment 362-410): the stream is the input elements with matching kept coords,
  row-major over the reduced dims. `nitems` given to `finalize_state` is `full_reduction_size`
  (463-466) for every cell, never a per-state count.
- `Op::new` / `new_array` return `Err`; the `Array::<op>()` methods `unwrap()` with `#[track_caller]`
  (common.rs:1385-1418, custom.rs:308-315). Kernels keep no shared mutable state; `Reduce`'s `F: Fn`.

### ReductionOpKernel contract (common.rs:20-114) - provided by kernels, relied on by the driver

- `init_state(Some((item, idx)))` seeds a lane or a cell from its first item; `idx` is `Some` iff
  `NEEDS_INDICES` (default `true` at 119; every kernel except ArgMax/ArgMin sets `false`) and is the
  row-major position in the reduced sub-shape. `init_state(None)` is called only from
  `finalize_states_empty_inner_loop` (1259-1269), i.e. only for `SUPPORTS_EMPTY` kernels.
- `update_state` folds the next item of the SAME lane, in ascending stream position; ArgMax/ArgMin
  keep the earlier item on ties (min_max.rs:61-68) and rely on it.
- `merge_states` must be associative + commutative over disjoint subsets (73-79); used for lane
  collapse (1017-1036), the pairwise tree (912-918) and cross-tile merges in the one-cell path (808-811).
  Arg merge breaks ties / NaN-vs-NaN by lower index (min_max.rs:70-76).
- `NEEDS_FINALIZE = false` is an unsafe promise (89-101): `Output` has `State`'s layout and
  `finalize_state` is the identity. Claimed by Max (min_max.rs:163), Min (237), Sum (arith.rs:408),
  Product (505), All (bools.rs:67), Any (135), Reduce (custom.rs:116) - all `Output = State` and
  return `state`. Consumed at common.rs:1149-1155. The trait is `pub(crate)`; only `Reduce`'s closure
  is user code.
- `PREFER_TREE_MERGE == false` folds a whole run as one leaf (899); true for float Sum/Mean
  (`!IS_PRECISE`), Var/Std and Reduce; false for Product (even float), Max/Min/Arg*, All/Any.
- `ONE_CELL_LANES` (115): `Some(8 on x86 / 16)` for ArgMax/ArgMin (min_max.rs:327, 403); otherwise
  derived from the SIMD width and `size_of State` (common.rs:819-834), clamped to [8, 1024], capped at
  `prev_power_of_two(4096 / max(size_of T, size_of State, 1))`, const-asserted power of two <= 512.

### Relied on from other modules

- `check_out_buf` (storage/buf.rs:352-364): `check_get_range` + `check_region_size` (32-bit only,
  error.rs:298-312) + for push `check_out_buf_impl` (384-431): stride count, writability, no overlap
  over len>1 dims, span <= buffer length. NOT alignment. The writable-`StridedBuf` contract
  (buf.rs:89-139) additionally forbids overlap with any input of the lazy chain (caller's duty, K31).
- `OutBuf::materialize` (buf.rs:475-488) -> `alloc_out_buf` (434-447): pooled, at the OUTPUT dtype
  alignment, strides from `strides_for_layout_order` (util/mod.rs:164-179). Pool memory is
  UNINITIALIZED (util/buf_pool.rs:39), and so is the tmp state buffer (503). In pull mode the slot is
  filled (`write_out_buf_slot`, buf.rs:505-515) at common.rs:353, before the fallible steps at 501/569.
- `inner_array.read_data_pull(&tile_index, ctx)` (569; core_trait.rs:167-175): bytes valid for the
  tile at the inner's own strides, possibly 0-strides (broadcast), possibly unaligned
  (core_trait.rs:88-92), holding valid `T` bit patterns (`bool8`: any byte).
- `read_shape_heuristic` (storage/params.rs:758-779) -> `scale_read_shape` (util/mod.rs:464-522):
  every dim of the scale order (all dims) clamped to `[1, max_shape]` (498-500), then grown up to
  `2 * read_size.max / itemsize` (weighted) or `read_size.min / itemsize`; a dim equal to its requested
  extent is snapped to `array_shape[d].max(1)` (532-536). `ReadSize` has no upper bound and is
  user-settable (params.rs:19-38, 189-192). The driver divides by `tile_shape[d]` for every dim (537).
- `calc_block_end` (util/mod.rs:621-629) and `NdIter::builder_with_begin` + `with_block_offset_size_ext`
  (util/iter/nd.rs:422-432, 497-513): blocks partition `[begin, end)` exactly in row-major order, each
  non-empty; an empty range yields nothing; a 0-dim iterator yields one item.
- `NdIterUnordered::new_with` (util/nd_iter_unordered.rs:64-172): drops len-1 dims (79-86); all-len-1 ->
  shape `[1]` with strides = layout sizes (87-97); any len-0 -> `[0]` (80-82); sort by per-operand
  stride, operand 0 first, a 0 stride abstains, operand 2 (logical index) excluded (106-125); coalesces
  only when ALL operands agree, the logical one included (134-148); outer walk ascending (214-306).
- `PtrNoalias`/`PtrMutNoalias` (util/mod.rs:669-772): `bytes_offset` needs `offset <= span`, `noalias`
  must be truthful. `REQUIRE_ALIGNED` (668-672) is false on x86/x86_64/aarch64, true elsewhere (armv7).
- Scalar ops: integer `Add`/`Mul` wrap (ops/elementwise/arith.rs:298, 312); `Maximum`/`Minimum` give a
  canonical NaN, either zero sign, `std::cmp::max/min` for bool8 (ops/elementwise/min_max.rs:10-95);
  `Cast` real->complex sets `im = +0.0` (ops/elementwise/cast.rs:181-190), bool8 -> number is 0/1 (64);
  bool8 `Eq`/`Ord` by truthiness, `&`/`|` normalize to 0/1 (scalar/bool.rs:44-62, 87-100);
  `map_vectors2` (scalar/simd.rs:208) for the Welford bulk path.
- No `read_as_elementwise_pipeline` override: inside an elementwise expression a reduction is a leaf
  read with `read_data_pull` (core_trait.rs:113-125) whose buffer the pipeline consumes unchecked
  (ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs:818) - so every output cell must be written.

## Unsafe inventory

- common.rs:492 `from_raw_parts_mut(out_ptr, out_buf_len)`: state buffer aliases the output when
  `state_in_out_buf` (485-491: same itemsize, state align <= output align, base and ALL out strides
  multiples of output align). Local; typed access later relies on the out-buffer contract.
- 567-568 `Index::new_unchecked(tile_start, tile_size)` (NEW, #103): needs non-zero sizes, ndim <= 8,
  no `start + size` overflow. Established by non-empty tiles inside the checked region, but sizes are
  `tile_size[d] as usize` (566), an unchecked u64 -> usize cast on 32-bit; only `debug_assert` inside.
- 579 `get_unchecked_mut(state_offset..)`: needs `state_offset <= state_buf.len()`. NON-LOCAL: tile
  containment is `debug_assert` only (558-564); tmp buffer is `out_nitems * state_size` packed (502,
  bounded by `check_region_size` 501 on 32-bit, by `new`'s shape check on 64-bit); out buffer span
  from `check_out_buf_impl` (push) or the pool allocation (pull).
- 737-738 `bytes_offset(item_offset / state_offset)`: offsets from `NdIterUnordered` over the tile
  with the items' and states' strides. NON-LOCAL: the inner pull buffer must span its strides.
- 807-812 one-cell `&mut *ptr.cast::<MaybeUninit<State>>()` then `assume_init_read` iff
  `base_item_idx > 0`: needs alignment (485-491 / 503; `debug_assert` only at 709-713) and that the
  cell was initialized earlier in THIS call. NON-LOCAL: visitation order (Hot spots 1).
- 935, 1100-1101 `assert_unchecked` on strides: 935 from `items_contiguous` (720); in the multi-cell
  contiguous path the strides are synthesized at 1080, so correctness rests on the flags at 729.
  1246-1247 is checked at 1211.
- 988, 990, 998-1009 item reads: CONTIGUOUS uses `read_maybe_aligned::<REQUIRE_ALIGNED>` (aligned
  read only after `items_aligned` 704-706 checked base + all coalesced strides); `[T; LANES]` reads need
  `i + LANES <= len` (callers pass multiples of LANES, 867); strided path uses `read_unaligned`.
- 1022-1035 lane collapse via `MaybeUninit`: each slot read once per level; "not panic-safe" (1022) -
  only `Reduce`'s closure can panic and states are `Copy`, so nothing is double-dropped.
- 1113-1123 multi-cell `&mut *states.add(i)` / `byte_add` (aligned reference) and `assume_init_read`
  when `!INIT`; `INIT` is `base_item_idx == 0` (637). NON-LOCAL, same as 807.
- 1173, 1175, 1185, 1252-1256, 1264-1267 finalize: raw pointer adds; `read_unaligned` of a state then
  `write_unaligned` of the output, possibly at the SAME address (aliasing detected by base-pointer
  equality, 1154) - sound only because each element is read before it is written and the strides are
  identical when aliased.
- Trait-level: `NEEDS_FINALIZE = false` (89-101), see Contracts. `ArrayStorageImpl` markers are empty.

## Edge-case surface

- Empty reduced dim (Sum/Product/All/Any only): `bulk_shape = 1`, `bulk_grid_end = calc_block_end(0,0,1)
  = 0`, no tiles; `finalize_states` writes `finalize(init_state(None), 0)` to every cell (1181-1187).
  Others error in `new` (147-158). Empty KEPT range cannot reach `read_data` (Index is non-empty).
- All dims reduced: 0-d output, `out_nitems = 1`, state strides all 0 -> one-cell path. 0-d input:
  only `dims = []`, `InnerD = DimDyn`; `NdIterUnordered` single-element case -> multi-cell with len 1.
- `dims = []`: `full_reduction_size = 1`; var gives 0 (ddof 0) or NaN (ddof >= 1).
- Single-element tile: state stride = state size, logical stride 1 -> multi-cell path, len 1 (the
  `debug_assert` at 723-726 depends on `inner_len == 1`).
- Broadcast input (0 item strides) on reduced or kept dims; the sort treats 0 as "no opinion". Push
  `out` with permuted, gapped, unaligned base or non-multiple strides falls back to a tmp state buffer
  + unaligned writes (tests `sum_into_misaligned_out_buf` common.rs:1996, `sum_into_strided_2d_output_
  multi_bulk` 2120, `var_into_strided_output_non_aliasing_state` 2198). A 0 stride in `out` is legal
  only on a len-1 dim (overlap check); such dims are dropped by `NdIterUnordered`.
- NDIM_MAX = 8; alignment: on i686 u64/f64 align to 4, so `(u64, T)` ArgMax states are 12/16 bytes.
- Dtypes: bool8 (Sum -> u64 counting non-zero bytes, Mean/Var -> f64, All/Any bool8-only, Max/Min/
  ArgMax by truthiness, no Product); f16 (Sum/Product accumulate in f16 scalar-only, Mean in f32 then
  f64, Var in f64); Complex (Sum, Product, Mean, Var, Std; no Max/Min/Arg*). Struct / inner-shape
  dtypes only via `Reduce` (State = T; lanes capped by width; K72 debug-build stack still open).
- Integer accumulators wrap silently: Sum/Product into i64/u64; Mean sums i8..i32 in i64, u8..u32/bool8
  in u64, i64/u64 in f64 (arith.rs:302-318).
- NaN/inf/-0.0: Max/Min canonical NaN; Arg* first NaN; `Sum::init` is `-0.0` (arith.rs:103-105) so a
  sum of `-0.0`s stays `-0.0`, but an empty sum is `+0.0` (385); Var of inf/NaN is NaN; `ddof = NaN`
  gives NaN (`denom > 0.0` false, variance.rs:158).
- 32-bit targets (x86, armv7 wheels): stream positions, logical strides and `idx` are u64 (471-482,
  574-576, 980-982; K86 fixed); tmp state size bounded (501; K85 fixed). Remaining usize casts:
  `tile_size as usize` (566), `inner_len as usize` (744), offsets `as usize` (737-738). Reduced extents
  > 2^32 are reachable with lazy broadcasts or compressible Compact arrays.

## Intentional behaviors

- Integer sum/product/mean-sum wrap and raise nothing (arith.rs:53-53, 144-147; error.rs:317-317);
  float reductions report no status either (K145, intended since #95).
- `sum(bool8)` -> u64 (NumPy int64) and `product(bool8)` unsupported (arith.rs:329, 338-341, 431-433;
  jix-py/python/tests/test_reduction.py:116-122).
- Accumulation width: Sum/Product keep float/complex width (f16 sums in f16; the Rust f16 sum/mean
  proptests are skipped, arith.rs:655, 754); Mean widens (f16 -> f32 state, f32 -> f64, Complex<f32>
  -> Complex<f64>, i64/u64 -> f64) and divides by a real count (arith.rs:291-298; K74 fixed); Var/Std
  accumulate in f64 (Complex<f64> mean for complex), output the real component type, and `std` takes
  the sqrt in f64 before narrowing (variance.rs:155-161, 216-288; K94 fixed).
- Reassociation: lane count, pairwise tree and tile merges depend on SIMD level, shape, block shape
  and read size (host cache sizes, K150 open), so float results differ in the last bits between paths
  and hosts (custom.rs:16-28). Float Product is never tree-merged (arith.rs:502). Variance's bulk path
  multiplies by `1/count` (variance.rs:201-207), the scalar path divides (99).
- Max/Min propagate NaN as the canonical NaN, either zero sign for +-0 (min_max.rs:91-93; ops/
  elementwise/min_max.rs:18-19). For bool8, Max/Min/Reduce return an input byte unchanged (a
  non-canonical true such as 2 can pass through) while All/Any normalize to 0/1 - an open question in
  run 2026-10-29-batch6 (section 6 of its report), not yet a finding.
- ArgMax/ArgMin: first NaN wins, earliest index on ties (min_max.rs:19-21, 247-250), output u64,
  single dim only (macro `single_dim`; multi-dim is crate-internal, `debug_assert` at common.rs:136-139).
- Empty reductions: Sum -> +0 (arith.rs:339, 385; test `sum_empty_float_is_positive_zero` arith.rs:729,
  K62 fixed), Product -> 1 (434), All -> true (bools.rs:10), Any -> false (77); every other kernel ->
  `Err` from `new`, panic from the `Array` method. The Mean doc "panics" (arith.rs:514) means the method.
- Complex seeds are not identities: `Sum` seeds `(-0.0, +0.0)` so a length-1 sum turns an imaginary
  `-0.0` into `+0.0`; `Product` seeds `(1, 0)` so `1+inf*i` over a length-1 dim gives `(NaN, inf)`.
  NumPy does the same bit for bit (batch5 REPORT.md:357, 587-589) - do not report.
- Var/Std: `n - ddof <= 0` -> NaN (variance.rs:73, 158, 299-302), even where NumPy gives inf.
  `m2 < 0.0` (overflow) -> +inf, a NaN m2 stays NaN (variance.rs:156; tests at 566-603). K108 (finite
  data whose Welford mean overflows, 3+ items -> NaN) is OPEN and known.
- Negative dims, `dim=None`, keepdim exist only in Python (jix-py/src/ops/reduction.rs:26-123,
  jix-py/src/util.rs:220-283); keepdim re-inserts via `InsertDim` output positions, which accepts
  unsorted dims (ops/shape_ops/insert_dim.rs:59-86). Python `argmax(dim=None)` works only for 1-D
  (util.rs:235-248; batch6 open question).
- `reduce_unordered` closures must be associative + commutative (custom.rs:16-28); each cell does
  exactly `n - 1` closure calls (test doc custom.rs:559-569).

## Hot spots

Changed since 6dbeb15 (concentrate here): common.rs:9-19 + 209-212 (cache ids, #100), 240-267
(`read_cached` + cache scope, #100/#104), 293-360 (`Index`, `OutBuf`, `materialize`, #103/#104),
412-430 (no early return; start/size/end region, #103), 494-508 (state strides, #103), 554-588
(`tile_start`, `Index::new_unchecked`, `read_data_pull`, #103/#104), 611. In consult files:
storage/buf.rs:352-515 (OutBuf, split `check_out_buf`), storage/index.rs (new), context.rs:144-290
(read cache), storage/params.rs:827-908 (cache ids). Kernel files: moved only.

1. Init vs merge is keyed ONLY on stream position: `init = base_item_idx == 0` (637) for multi-cell,
   `base_item_idx > 0` -> merge with the stored state (808) for one-cell. The argument: the first tile
   of each bulk starts at reduced coords 0 (tile grid row-major from `bulk_begin`), `NdIterUnordered`
   walks outer positions ascending from 0, logical strides are >= 1 on every reduced dim of len > 1,
   and reduced/kept dims never coalesce (logical operand). Can any layout break one of these (len-1
   reduced dims, broadcast reduced dims, reduced dims in reverse memory order, permuted out strides,
   a kept tile starting mid-block, the single-element case, a zero-sized tile)?
2. One-cell vs multi-cell is `state_inner_stride == 0` (717). It relies on push `out` never having a
   0 stride on a len>1 dim (`check_out_buf_impl`); the cache-hit path checks `out` separately
   (context.rs:188-190). Is there an internal caller that builds a writable out without that check?
3. Stream positions: `tile_base_reduced_idx` (574-576), per-run base from the logical operand (740),
   lane indices + `idx_step` (939-966), tail indices (875). Do ArgMax/ArgMin pick the first max across
   lanes, tails, pairwise halves and tiles, with NaN anywhere?
4. `state_in_out_buf` (485-491) + in-place finalize (1153-1180): every kernel passing the size/align
   test must be safe to finalize in place (Mean<f64>, Mean<i8..u32/bool8> i64/u64 state -> f64 out,
   Mean<Complex<f64>>). Does the early return at 1155 ever skip a needed write?
5. Path agreement: contiguous one-cell uses runtime SIMD + `K::ONE_CELL_LANES`/SIMD lanes, strided
   uses baseline + 16 lanes (798-806, 825-840); multi-cell contiguous synthesizes strides (1080);
   Sum/Product `update_bulk_simd` falls back to scalar on Sse2/Neon or for wide casts (arith.rs:16-46).
6. NEW: tile size casts. `tile_size[d] as usize` (566) feeds `Index::new_unchecked` (567) and the fold
   (`inner_len as usize`, 744). On 32-bit a reduced-dim tile can exceed u32 when the user's
   `read_size` is huge (no upper bound); what happens to NonZero, dropped items and later
   `assume_init_read`s?
7. NEW: error after materialize. `check_region_size` (501, 32-bit) and the inner read (569) can fail
   after the pull slot was filled with an uninitialized pooled buffer (359); `read_cached_impl`
   (context.rs:210) propagates with `?`. Does any caller inspect or reuse a slot after an `Err`?
8. NEW: read cache. The reduction result is cached per (id, start, size) when used twice in one outer
   expression; inner reads are cached per tile inside `self.cache_scope`. Is the cached buffer ever
   handed to a consumer that expects a writable or exclusive pull buffer? Does eviction
   (`return_shared`, util/buf_pool.rs:59-63) ever recycle a buffer still borrowed by `items`?
9. Variance: `welford_update_bulk` (variance.rs:190-214) vs scalar `update` (95-103); complex split
   into re/im passes sharing `m2` (173-187); `merge_states` with count 0 (128-134) and complex
   `delta * Complex(r, 0)` (140-143); finalize uses `nitems`, not `state.count` (157).
10. Kernel seeds: `init_state(Some(x))` is `init op x` (arith.rs:379-384, 475-481, 558-564;
    variance.rs:347-353; bools.rs:47-53, 115-121) - exact for reals; complex is intentional (above).

### Suspicions (unverified)

- [CONFIRMED in batch7-1 as K153] common.rs:560-562 - on 32-bit, `tile_size[d] as usize` truncates a reduced-dim tile longer than
  2^32 (only with a user `read_size` above ~4 GiB * itemsize); a result of 0 breaks `Index`'s
  `NonZeroUsize` invariant (`new_unchecked`, debug_assert only) and skips the first tile, so the next
  tile's `assume_init_read` (809 / 1121) reads an uninitialized state; a non-zero truncation drops items.
- [CONFIRMED in batch7-3 as K165] common.rs:2399-2407 (test-only) - the 32-bit-only test passes `&[0..n]` to `read_data_pull`, which
  now takes `&Index`, so this test module no longer compiles for 32-bit targets (CI never builds 32-bit
  tests), hiding the K85/K86 regression tests.
